review: Excellent game, great fun. I have one quibble so far: Making an in-app purchase is not an achievement, and to add it to the achievements list is just a tad manipulative. It's not a good look and you might want to consider taking it out.

WARNING: THIS GAME WILL REMOVE MAPS THAT YOU BOUGHT WITHOUT WARNING. I paid for map packs which contained Moscow and Russia maps and seemingly overnight the maps disappeared without a trace. This is likely Hasbro or SMG Studio trying to do some sort of performative "activism" to protest the war in Ukraine, when in reality deleting maps does absolutely NOTHING to stop the war, but DOES cheat their customers out of the hard earned money they spent. I STILL HAVE NOT BEEN REIMBURSED.

I really liked this game because it's addictive and fun, but I cannot in good faith recommend that anyone buy any additional content from this game besides playing the maps that are free, because according to the standard set, you could easily loose maps you have purchased in the blink of an eye.

I will not be purchasing any more content from this game until the developers reimburse me/ reinstate the maps, and then prove that this will not happen again.

The game was coded by 12 year olds, competitive issues that have existed for over 4 years continue to exist. Exploits go unpatched month after month. Too stupid to figure out how to end a stalemate? Too braindead to attempt to ally yourself with someone to knock the other player out? Fear not you can just pretend to bot out and let the other 2 players smack each other because they think your just a bot now. But then 10 minutes later you rejoin completely ignored and untouched and get your free win. In case you thought E.A. didn't influence the gaming market worry not friends, you can spend 8 buck for the new map pack that is released every 3 months of which maybe 1 map is even played once in a blue moon but most of the time none of them are played. At this point that means spending over 300$ to get every single map. But don't worry technically 70% of games are played over 6 different map packs options so you technically only need to spend 80$ on the game you already bought. For those who want some positivity though, 3 years later they finally 'fixed' balanced blitz dice. Must have been one hell of a problem to take 3 years to 'fix'

24 May 2024 edit:

I purchased the Viking Legends Map Pack via the RISK: All Access bundle on Steam two days ago ($3.19 USD), but my content has yet to unlock in game - maps are present in the in-game list, but still display the padlock icon. This is reminiscent of issues SMG had over two years ago, before they decided to sever specific content from the bundle. Steam says the DLC is installed. What do I need to do to play content I've already paid for? I shouldn't have to jump through hoops to do so.

4 Mar 2024 edit:

I purchased the Steam All Access Bundle and have typically bought new map content on the day of release at a small discount but still substantial cumulative cost. Prior to release of the Dune Map Pack the pack WAS listed in the bundle ("22 of 23 items from this collection are already in your library") but without a price. When I logged in today I discover that it's no longer in the "All Access" bundle (the bundle name has to have quotes now) nor the price of similar map packs ($3.99) - it's now standalone only and at 150% the normal price.

I get economics. I also get good business. To violate the expectations of consumers who for years have relied on an "All Access" product to be just that, to raise prices for a small DLC map pack to a cost for which one can sometimes get a decent full game (and at a cumulative price the most computationally expensive, complex, and popular games seldom reach), and all this simply because of hype is sort of a slap in the face to the loyal player base. 

Unless SMG Studio can provide a decent explanation for this, I won't be buying, as much as I'd otherwise like to and had intended to. Please don't say something like "It's a limited time offer - we have to recoup cost faster" or "We are licensing this and have to share the revenue"; the development overhead for a product functioning like this has to be incredibly low (the rendering of the maps?) and if Dune did nothing more than generate interest at cost for the platform it would still be a win for SMG. Had this release been approached normally you'd have more of my money and time. As it is you have only my dissatisfaction and more resentment than probably either of us feel is warranted.

I'd like to change my review back to "Recommended". I've changed my reviews in the past when SMG did the right thing. Please convince me by doing it again.
